papers.name: Component Group 1 Period study with non-British depth study

topics.name: Period study: International Relations: the changing international order 1918–1975
points: Conflict and co-operation 1918–1939: successes and failures of internationalism in the 1920s; retreat to nationalism in the 1930s
The Versailles Peace Settlement
The League of Nations in the 1920s; Dawes Plan, Locarno, Kellogg-Briand Pact, Young Plan; attempts at disarmament
Impact of the worldwide economic depression; failure of the League in the 1930s
European tensions in the 1930s: Appeasement and the outbreak of war in 1939
Historical controversy: changing interpretations of Appeasement
The Cold War in Europe 1945–1961: Yalta and Potsdam; Soviet actions in Eastern Europe 1945–48 and Western responses
Division of Germany; Truman Doctrine and Marshall Plan; Berlin Blockade and Airlift
Development of NATO and the Warsaw Pact; building of the Berlin Wall 1961 and its effects
Cold War confrontations 1954–1975: the Cuban Missile Crisis 1962
Vietnam: origins of US involvement 1954–65; US and Vietcong tactics and their consequences
Vietnam: US withdrawal, American opposition to the war, end of the war and its impact on international relations
Historical controversy: changing interpretations of the responsibility for the Cold War

topics.name: Non-British depth study: China 1950–1981: The People and the State
points: Establishing Communism 1950–1965: purges of opposition in the early 1950s; the Hundred Flowers campaign
Mao's social policies: women, young people and education; contrast with Chinese traditionalism
Agricultural policy: land reform and collectivisation; industrial policy and the First Five Year Plan
The Great Leap Forward: effects on society and reasons for failure; Dazhai Commune as a case study
The Cultural Revolution 1966–1976: reasons; impact on intellectuals and students; the Red Guards
The impact of Communism in Tibet
Communist propaganda and Mao's personality cult; Dazhai and Party repression
After Mao 1976–1981: the Gang of Four, the 'democracy wall' and treatment of opposition
Deng Xiaoping's economic changes and the Four Modernisations
Social change under Deng: women, education, the One Child policy; propaganda

topics.name: Non-British depth study: Germany 1925–1955: The People and the State
points: Strengths and weaknesses of the Weimar Republic 1925–1928; Nazi policies and position in 1928
Impact of the Depression; political, social and economic crisis 1929–1933; rising Nazi support
Consolidation of power 1933–34: Reichstag Fire, March 1933 elections, Enabling Act, the army, elimination of opposition and the SA
The terror state: SA, SS, Gestapo, SD, courts and police
Culture and propaganda; Hitler's personal popularity; the National Community
Economic policies and their winners and losers; policies towards women and youth
Lack of effective opposition; persecution of Jews, Roma, Jehovah's Witnesses and homosexuals; eugenics
War 1939–1945: reaction to war, early gains, eastern colonisation, bombing, support and opposition
Escalating racial persecution and the Holocaust
Defeat, occupation and de-Nazification; differing experiences in East and West Germany 1945–1955

topics.name: Non-British depth study: South Africa 1960–1994: The People and the State
points: Consolidation of Apartheid: Separate Development and the Bantustans; support for Apartheid; methods of maintaining the regime
The Sharpeville Massacre and its impact
Resistance in the 1960s: ANC, Freedom Charter, Umkhonto we Sizwe, Poqo; the Rivonia Trial 1964
Black Consciousness Movement, SASO and women's groups
Trade unions and the 1973 Durban strikes; young people and the 1976 Soweto uprising
The ANC in exile and the international Anti-Apartheid Movement; the regime's response to resistance
Collapse of apartheid: sanctions, United Democratic Front and mass resistance; Inkatha and violence
The 1983 constitution and the State of Emergency 1985–1990; failure of 'total strategy' and Cuito Cuanavale
Roles of de Klerk, Ramaphosa and Mandela; unbanning of the ANC, PAC and SACP; negotiations
The first free elections in 1994

topics.name: Non-British depth study: The USA 1919–1948: The People and the State
points: The 'Roaring Twenties': Republican policies; industries and groups that did and did not prosper
Women's rights and the Sheppard-Towner Act
Prohibition: causes, aims, implementation and failure
Prejudice and discrimination: Jim Crow laws, Ku Klux Klan, Red Scare, Palmer Raids, Sacco and Vanzetti, immigration restriction
Combating prejudice: the NAACP and UNIA
The Great Depression: economic and social effects; government response; the 1932 election
The First New Deal: the Hundred Days and the Alphabet Agencies
The Second New Deal: WPA, Social Security Act, Wagner Act; reactions to and impact of the New Deals
Second World War: mobilisation, propaganda, war production, expanded government power, social impact, women
Japanese internment; Detroit Race Riots 1943; Executive Order 8802 and desegregation of the military 1948

topics.name: Non-British depth study: The USA 1945–1974: The People and the State
points: Post-war concern about Communist influence; the late-1940s Red Scare, J Edgar Hoover and the Rosenbergs
McCarthyism: nature, support and opposition
Position of African Americans 1945–1954: Jim Crow, education, voting and employment
Brown v. Board of Education 1954 and the Montgomery Bus Boycott
Martin Luther King's leadership; roles of SNCC, SCLC and NAACP
Opposition to civil rights; roles of the Supreme Court, Kennedy and Johnson; the Civil Rights Act 1964
Malcolm X and Black Power; campaigns for Native American and Chicano rights
Feminism: Betty Friedan, NOW, Equal Pay Act, Status Commission, 1972 Supreme Court ruling
The Stonewall riots 1969
Divisions: anti-Vietnam War protests, anti-poverty campaigns, the Great Society and Nixon's welfare pledges

topics.name: Thematic study: Migration to Britain c.1000 to c.2010
points: c.1000–1500: population diversity before 1066; impact of the Norman Conquest
c.1000–1500: Jews in England from 1066 to the expulsion of 1290
c.1000–1500: medieval immigrants ('aliens'): lives, impact, treatment and integration
c.1500–1900: Africans in 16th-century England
c.1500–1900: arrivals from the Indian subcontinent via the East India Company: lascars, servants, ayahs
c.1500–1900: African communities, the Royal African Company and the slave trade
c.1500–1900: readmission of the Jews 1656; Protestant refugees and Huguenots from the 1670s
c.1500–1900: Irish and Scottish migrants in the Industrial Revolution; Eastern European Jews; the 1870 Naturalisation Act
1900–c.2010: diverse port communities; Aliens Act 1905, Status of Aliens Act 1914, British Nationality Act 1948
1900–c.2010: Jewish refugees in the 1930s; migrants in the World Wars; Polish settlers after 1945
1900–c.2010: Commonwealth migration, racism and anti-racism, race relations and immigration controls 1962 and 1981
1900–c.2010: multicultural society, asylum seekers and refugees, EU free movement c.1990–c.2010

topics.name: Thematic study: Power: Monarchy and Democracy in Britain c.1000 to 2014
points: c.1000–c.1485: Anglo-Saxon kingship, royal power and the thegns
c.1000–c.1485: claims to the throne in 1066 and the Norman monarchy to 1087
c.1000–c.1485: King John and Magna Carta; early Parliament and Simon de Montfort
c.1000–c.1485: deposition of Richard II 1399; the Wars of the Roses
c.1485–c.1800: Tudor government; royal power and Parliament under Henry VIII and Elizabeth I
c.1485–c.1800: Charles I's Personal Rule, the Civil Wars, abolition of monarchy and the Restoration 1660
c.1485–c.1800: James II, the Glorious Revolution 1688, Bill of Rights, parties and parliamentary monarchy
c.1800–2014: Reform Acts 1832, 1867, 1884; trade unions, the Labour Party and women's suffrage
c.1800–2014: wartime government control and the expanding role of the state after 1945
c.1800–2014: challenges to Parliament: Miners' Strike, CND, Greenpeace; Thatcher and Blair; devolution; coalition government

topics.name: Thematic study: War and British Society c.790 to c.2010
points: c.790–c.1500: Viking raids on Anglo-Saxon England and responses
c.790–c.1500: the Norman Conquest, resistance and the feudal system
c.790–c.1500: feudal society c.1100–1215; breakdowns under Stephen and John
c.790–c.1500: medieval war c.1290–c.1450: feudal service, cost and impact on the population
c.1500–c.1750: Elizabeth I's wars with Spain, Parliament and privateers; warfare on the Scottish borders
c.1500–c.1750: the Civil Wars 1642–51 in England, Scotland and Ireland; the Jacobite Wars 1715 and 1745
c.1750–c.2010: imperial wars including the Seven Years War; Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars
c.1750–c.2010: the Crimean War and the Boer Wars
c.1750–c.2010: the First and Second World Wars as total war; state power and the people
c.1750–c.2010: post-1945 conflicts: Cold War Britain, the IRA campaigns 1969–94, Iraq War 2003, terrorism

papers.name: Component Group 3 British depth study with study of the historic environment

topics.name: British depth study: The Impact of Empire on Britain 1688–c.1730
points: The Glorious Revolution and Hanoverian succession; England's position in the British Isles
Military campaigns in Ireland 1688–91 and the settlement that followed
England and Scotland after 1688: Jacobites, Massacre of Glencoe 1692, Darien Scheme, Act of Union 1707, the 1715 Rebellion
Emigration, including forced emigration, from the British Isles to the Americas
Economic impact of war and empire; the Bank of England 1694
Trade with India and China; the East India Company in Kolkata
End of the Royal African Company monopoly 1698; Treaty of Utrecht 1713; South Sea Bubble
Importance of the North American and Caribbean colonies; the slave-based economy
Rise of consumerism; slave trade ports (Bristol, Liverpool, London)
Ideas of racial hierarchy and settled minority communities; opposition to slavery and slave resistance
Political activism and the role of coffee houses

topics.name: British depth study: The English Reformation c.1520–c.1550
points: The role and wealth of the Church c.1520; religious practice and the Church and people
Influence of Lollard and Lutheran ideas; critics of the Church and popular attitudes to reform
Henry VIII's annulment and the Reformation Parliament 1529–34
Thomas Cromwell, the Valor Ecclesiasticus and the Visitation of the Monasteries
The process of Dissolution and the Suppression Acts 1536 and 1539; reactions
Effects of the Dissolution on religious orders, the poor and culture
Resistance: the Lincolnshire Rising and the Pilgrimage of Grace 1536–37
Religious policy under Henry VIII and Edward VI; changes to worship, prayer books and the English Bible
Impact on church fabric and clergy; enforcement and responses of ordinary people
The Prayer Book Rebellion 1549

topics.name: British depth study: Personal Rule to Restoration 1629–1660
points: Why Charles I summoned Parliament in 1640; the Long Parliament's criticisms of Personal Rule
Attacks on Laud and Strafford; divisions within Parliament 1640–42
The road to civil war: Irish rebellion, Grand Remonstrance, Five Members, Militia Ordinance, Nineteen Propositions
Attempts at agreement with Charles I 1646–47, including the Propositions of Newcastle
Parliament and radical groups: Levellers, Quakers, Diggers
Parliament and the Army: Presbyterians and Independents
The execution of Charles I and the Rump's Republic 1649
The Rump and Cromwell 1649–53; the Instrument of Government and the Major Generals
The Humble Petition and Advice and Cromwell's response
Attempts at settlement 1658–60 and the Restoration of the monarchy

topics.name: Study of the historic environment: Urban Environments: Patterns of Migration (Spitalfields), with The Impact of Empire
points: When immigrant groups arrived in Spitalfields, why and from where
How immigrants were received by settled populations and authorities
The experiences of immigrants: housing, welfare, work, faith and community organisations
Key events in local migration history and how they are commemorated
The impact of migration on the area: economic, social, political and cultural

topics.name: Study of the historic environment: Castles: Form and Function c.1000–1750 (Kenilworth Castle), with The English Reformation or Personal Rule to Restoration
points: The location of Kenilworth Castle: strategic and physical setting
Appearance and layout of Kenilworth Castle at different times, including slighting
Day-to-day functions of Kenilworth Castle: conquest, baronial and royal power, administration, residence
Life in Kenilworth Castle at different times: owners and those who ran it
Key events associated with Kenilworth Castle: rebellions, sieges and civil war
